title: She moved to America at 20 with $200. Now she's building the world's longest-range electric boat.

sources.text: Robb Report - How Sampriti Bhattacharyya Launched a Top U.S. Boatbuilding Company

caption:
She moved to America at 20 with $200. Now she's building the world's longest-range electric boat.

Born in Kolkata, she moved to the US at 20 with just $200 and later earned a PhD in Mechanical Engineering from MIT in 2017, with career stops at NASA, Fermilab and TIFR. Her first venture, Hydroswarm, an ocean-robot startup, didn't succeed - she founded Navier in 2019 anyway.

Navier's N30 is the world's longest-range electric vessel, gliding four feet above the water on carbon foils that cut drag and wake while boosting speed. It runs roughly ten times more efficiently than a comparable gas-powered boat, in an industry Bhattacharyya sees as still running on legacy fleets.

A Viksit Bharat by 2047 needs builders who treat failure as data, not verdict. Bhattacharyya's first company folded - her second is now reshaping an entire industry most people assumed couldn't change.
